name: How do ADU bathroom permits affect the project timeline?

mainEntity.name: What parts of the bathroom permit process usually slow down ADU construction in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What parts of the bathroom permit process usually slow down ADU construction in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom permits can affect the project timeline more than homeowners expect because the bathroom touches plumbing, electrical, ventilation, waterproofing, and sometimes structural work. If the plan set is incomplete or the bathroom layout changes after submittal, plan check often sends corrections that add weeks. In ADU projects, the bathroom is frequently tied to sewer routing and utility coordination, so the permit review may depend on details that are not obvious on the first draft. To keep the schedule moving, the contractor or designer should coordinate fixture locations, venting, and drain paths before submitting plans. It also helps to choose finish details early enough to avoid late design changes. When the bathroom is simple and the plumbing path is clear, permits tend to move more smoothly. When the bathroom is complex, the schedule should include extra time for corrections and resubmittals. Homeowners should ask upfront which parts of the bathroom are already fully coordinated and which parts are still being decided.
acceptedAnswer.description: Bathroom permits can slow an ADU project when the plumbing, structural, or electrical plans are incomplete or when the bathroom layout changes after submittal. Corrections often happen if the drain route, venting, waterproofing details, or fixture locations are not coordinated early. The cleanest drawings usually get through review faster.
